Surah al-Munafiqun (The Hypocrites) [Meccan, and its verses are eleven]

﴿When the hypocrites come to you, they say﴾ with their tongues, contrary to what is in their hearts, ﴿"We testify that you are truly the Messenger of Allah." And Allah knows that you are truly His Messenger, and Allah testifies﴾ knows ﴿that the hypocrites are liars﴾ in what they conceal, contrary to what they say.

﴿They have taken their oaths as a shield﴾, a cover over their wealth and their lives, ﴿and so they averted [others] by them from the way of Allah﴾, i.e., from jihad (striving in the way of Allah, here armed fighting) with them.

ذَلِكَ (That) — i.e., their evil deeds — بِأَنَّهُمْ آمَنُوا (because they believed) with the tongue, ثُمَّ كَفَرُوا (then disbelieved) in the heart — i.e., they persisted in their disbelief in Him — فَطُبِعَ (so a seal was set) — i.e., it was sealed — عَلى قُلُوبهمْ (upon their hearts) with disbelief, فَهُمْ لا يَفْقُهُونَ (so they do not understand) faith.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 63, verse 4:

﴿And when you see them, their bodies please you﴾ by their beauty, ﴿and if they speak, you listen to their speech﴾ for its eloquence, ﴿as though they were﴾ because of the bulk of their bodies, in their lack of understanding, ﴿propped-up planks﴾ (read with the shin both sunken and with damma), ﴿leaned﴾ against the wall. ﴿They think every cry﴾ that is shouted, such as a call in the army or the recital of a lost item, ﴿is against them﴾ because of the terror in their hearts, that something will descend upon them that makes their blood lawful to shed. ﴿They are the enemy, so beware of them﴾ for they spread your secrets to the disbelievers. ﴿May Allah destroy them﴾, i.e. destroy them, ﴿how are they deluded?﴾ How are they turned away from faith after the proof has been established?

﴿When it is said to them, "Come, the Messenger of Allah will ask forgiveness for you,"﴾ [they make excuses]. ﴿They turn their heads﴾, [lawwū, read with] intensification (tashdīd) and with lightening (takhfīf) [as two recitations], meaning they inclined them away. ﴿And you see them turning away﴾, meaning they turn away from that.

﴿It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them﴾. The interrogative hamza (*hamzat al-istifham*, the hamza used to form a question) has been used in place of the connective hamza (*hamzat al-wasl*, the hamza pronounced at the start of a word when it is preceded by another word). Thus "أسْتَغْفَرْت" is read with the interrogative hamza.

ُ**﴿They are the ones who say﴾** to their companions from the Helpers (al-Anṣār), **﴿Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God﴾** from the Emigrants (al-Muhājirūn), **﴿until they disperse﴾**, i.e., until they scatter away from him. **﴿And to God belong the treasuries of the heavens and the earth﴾**, meaning the provision; so He is the Provider for the Emigrants and others.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 63, verse 8:

﴿They say: "If we return to Medina, the more honourable will surely expel the more humble from it."﴾ That is, from the expedition against Banu al-Mustaliq. By "the more honourable" they meant themselves, and by "the more humble" they meant the believers. ﴿But honour belongs to Allah, and to His Messenger, and to the believers; but the hypocrites do not know﴾ that.
O you who have believed! Let not your wealth or your children divert you (lā tulhikum: tashghalukum, "occupy you") from the remembrance of God, meaning the five prayers.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 63, verse 10:

﴿And spend﴾ in zakat ﴿out of what We have provided you before death comes to one of you, and he says: "My Lord, if only You would delay me to a near term, so I would give charity and be among the righteous"﴾ — here "lawla" means "halla" (why not), or the "la" is extra, and "law" is for wishing. ﴿…delay me to a near term, so I would give charity﴾ — the "ta" in its original form is assimilated into the "sad," so it reads "atasaddaq," meaning I would give zakat in charity. ﴿…and be among the righteous﴾ — by performing Hajj. Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "No one falls short in zakat and Hajj except that he asks to return at the time of death."
﴿And Allah will never delay a soul when its term has come, and Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾ Read with the letter التاء (al-tāʾ) and the letter الياء (al-yāʾ).
